notes: This episode required by far the most correction of the series so far, centered on an extended back-and-forth involving Krzysztof Gonciarz, Krzysztof Stanowski, and especially Maja Staśko (184 mentions -- by far the most of any single figure across all processed episodes), whose name appears in dozens of inflected forms, typos, and direct addresses ('Maju', 'Majśko', 'Maja Stezko', 'ma i Saśko', 'majusku', etc.). The naive draft's first validator pass alone produced roughly 75 Rule C misses, almost all of these variants. A subtlety arose partway through: after adding a genuine recurring chant-echo ('Mają wiem, że jesteśmy na...', repeated several times immediately after 'Maja Staśko') as an accepted target, the validator began flagging ~8 wholly unrelated, coincidental uses of the ordinary Polish verb 'mają' ('they have') elsewhere in the transcript. Each was checked in context and confirmed to be the common verb, not the name, and left unmarked -- while one genuine lowercase instance ('kontaktu z mają Staśką') was caught and correctly added. A full line-by-line read of the entire ~2-hour transcript then found roughly 140 further real misses: secondary figures (Dariusz Matecki, Karolina Domaracka, Marcin Kozak, Jakub Dymek, Anna Maria Żukowska, Maria Sadowska, Jaś Kapela, Kryspin Sobczak, Piolo), many multi-line surname splits, and numerous heavily garbled ASR forms resolved from context (e.g. 'Marazka' and 'Maradancka' for 'Domaracka', 'Pczłek' for 'Pączek', 'kozakowi' for 'Kozak'). The three recurring 'nazwijmy go Maciek' placeholder instances were correctly tagged to entity 124 rather than the real 'Maciej' (id 78). One residual false positive is expected and documented: 'Chris' at [58:52] is a substring of 'Christopher' in an unrelated list of real predators (Weinstein, Cosby, R. Kelly), not a reference to Krzysztof Gonciarz's alias.
